newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Taiwan sells unusually large three diesel cargoes.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan sells unusually large three diesel cargoes.

text.p: Taiwan's state-owned Chinese Petroleum Corp (CPC) has awarded three diesel cargoes for sale in its regular monthly tender for December lifting, a CPC official said on Friday.

The 0.3-percent sulphur cargoes, which are 225,000-to-250,000-barrels each are for December 11-30 lifting and were awarded to three traders around $30.00 per barrel free-on-board (fob) Kaoshiung, the official said.
Trading sources said the cargoes were awarded to German trader Stinnes, Singapore trader Hin Leong and Swiss trader Glencore at $29.92 per barrel fob, but this was not confirmed.
CPC usually sells one or two cargoes in its monthly sale tenders.
The CPC official said that the company was selling more than its usual volumes because of higher refinery runs.
"We are running the refineries at about 80-90 percent," he said. CPC normally runs its refineries at about 80 pecent of capacity.
"We raised output...(because) refining profit margin is good," he added.

The recent surge in diesel prices, which earlier this week traded at a new five-year high of $30.80 a barrel fob Singapore, has made it lucrative for refiners to raise their output especially for middle distillates.
In its last tender, CPC sold only one 225,000-to-250,000-barrel cargo also at $29.92 per barrel for November 11-30 lifting.
